draft.rationale: This session stays narrow: retrieve the respiration sequence and glycolysis, connect them in one map, verify against evidence, then repair any gap revealed by the learner's own attempt.

coverage.focus: Overall sequence of cellular respiration and glycolysis as the first stage
essentialIdeas: Glycolysis comes first in cellular respiration.
The Krebs cycle comes after glycolysis and before the electron transport chain.
completionEvidence: Attempt each target without notes and correct any exposed gap

methodBriefing.name: Concept Mapping
methodBriefing.what: You will recall the key stages, connect them with labeled relationships, check one claim against the completion rule, and then repair any missing link.
methodBriefing.why: This fits a short conceptual learning study because the target is the order and location of linked biology ideas, not a long fact list.
how: First answer from memory with the source closed.
Then connect the named stages with explicit relationship phrases.
Check the result against the required evidence.
If a gap appears, fix only that gap and retry.
methodBriefing.completion: The session is complete when both targets are attempted without notes, the concept map is built, the evidence check is answered, and any exposed gap is repaired.
personalization: YOVA is using the current task and session objective as the starting point until your completed work provides more evidence.

activities.label: Try
activities.title: Order from memory
activities.body: Write the three main stages of cellular respiration in order, without notes.
activities.correctAnswer: Glycolysis first, then the Krebs cycle, then the electron transport chain.
activities.feedback: Check the order only. The key idea is that glycolysis starts the process, the Krebs cycle follows, and the electron transport chain comes last.

activities.label: Map
activities.title: Connect glycolysis
activities.body: Connect the named ideas with relationship phrases.

methodRuntime.instructions: Connect the named concepts with the relationship phrases that show order and location.

connections.prompt: What is the relationship between cellular respiration and glycolysis?
connections.expectedRelationship: Glycolysis is the first stage of cellular respiration.
The Krebs cycle comes after glycolysis.

connections.prompt: What stage comes after the Krebs cycle?
connections.expectedRelationship: The electron transport chain comes after the Krebs cycle.

activities.correctAnswer: Glycolysis is the first stage of cellular respiration. Glycolysis occurs in the cytoplasm. The Krebs cycle comes after glycolysis. The electron transport chain comes after the Krebs cycle.
activities.feedback: The map should show both order and location. Glycolysis belongs in the cytoplasm and sits at the start of the cellular respiration sequence.

activities.label: Check
activities.title: Match the evidence
activities.body: Choose the statement that best matches the required evidence for this session.
choices: Read the notes once and then answer from memory.
Attempt both targets without notes and correct any exposed gap.
Copy the diagram and submit it without explanation.
Review the whole chapter before trying again.
activities.correctAnswer: Attempt both targets without notes and correct any exposed gap.
activities.feedback: The correct evidence is a closed-note attempt followed by correction of any gap. That is what shows the sequence and glycolysis were actually retrieved, not just reread.

activities.label: Fix
activities.title: Repair the glycolysis gap
activities.body: If your first answer missed glycolysis, correct it now in one sentence.
activities.correctAnswer: Glycolysis is the first stage of cellular respiration, and it happens in the cytoplasm.
activities.feedback: Use the corrected fact, not the earlier miss. The repair is complete when the location and sequence are both stated correctly.
